title: How to surpass no-go limits in Gaussian quantum error correction and entangled Gaussian state distillation

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Eq. (15) gives σ_L² → (2σ²/√π) ln(π^{1.5}/(2σ⁴)), while Eq. (16) gives σ_L² → e^{-2r}(2σ²/√π) √(4r + ln(π^{1.5}/(2σ⁴))). Eq. (16) is supposed to be obtained from Eq. (15) by the substitution σ² → e^{-2r}σ²; that substitution yields e^{-2r}(2σ²/√π)(4r + ln(π^{1.5}/(2σ⁴))) with NO square root. Hence either (15) is missing a square root (as in the Noh et al. asymptotic form) or (16) has a spurious one; the two equations are mutually inconsistent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Eq. (17) ('This concatenation is useful when 4/ln(π^{1.5}/(2σ⁴)) + 1 < e^{4r}')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Comparing Eq. (16) with Eq. (15) gives the usefulness condition 4r/ln(π^{1.5}/(2σ⁴)) + 1 < e^{4r}; the factor r is missing in the numerator as written. Moreover, as written the condition is self-contradictory with the sentence that follows: at r → 0⁺ the left-hand side 4/L + 1 is strictly greater than 1 = e^{0}, so the inequality fails for small r, contradicting the claim that 'this concatenation always yields benefits for r > 0'.

predicted_errors.error_location: Sentence after Eq. (17): 'For typical noise levels satisfying σ² < π³/(4√(2e)) ≈ 1.012'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: π³/(4√(2e)) = 31.0/(4·2.332) ≈ 3.32, not 1.012. The quoted numerical value 1.012 corresponds to π^{3/4}/√(2e) = 2.3597/2.3317 ≈ 1.012, which is also the correct threshold obtained from requiring ln(π^{1.5}/(2σ⁴)) ≥ 1. The displayed expression therefore contradicts its own numerical value and the derivation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Eq. (13) in the proof of Lemma 4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Eq. (13) is written as γ(ρ) → Z_i M Z_i γ(ρ) Z_i M Z_i + Z_i N Z_i. Applying the stated map γ → MγM^T + N conjugated by Z_i gives (Z_i M Z_i) γ (Z_i M Z_i)^T + Z_i N Z_i, i.e. the second factor must be Z_i M^T Z_i. The transpose is missing, so the displayed transformation is not the one claimed in Lemma 4 (nor does it preserve symmetry of γ in general).

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix B, definition of the displacement operator
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper defines D̂(α) = e^{αâ†−α*â} with q̂ = (â+â†)/√2, p̂ = (â−â†)/(i√2). Expanding gives αâ† − α*â = i√2(Im{α} q̂ − Re{α} p̂). Appendix B instead states D̂_j(α) = e^{i√2(Im{α} q̂_j + Re{α} p̂_j)}, i.e. with the wrong sign on the Re{α} p̂_j term (this sign then propagates into Eqs. (B9), (B17) and (C5)).

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 5 and Eq. (14) (definition of the map B_i)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: B_i maps G^{M,N} to G^{Z_iMZ_i, Z_iNZ_i} with Z_iMZ_i explicitly non-symplectic (the paper notes this), i.e. partial transposition is not a completely positive, physically realizable operation. In Theorem 5 these non-CP maps are freely composed with the noisy channels N^{σ²} as if they were ordinary channel elements. The gate-teleportation identity (Lemma 3) only establishes an identity for a factorized ideal EPR resource acting on a state; it does not justify inserting a partial transposition in the middle of a channel sequence where the data mode is already correlated with the channel environment. The proof therefore does not establish that the stated composite channel is implementable.

Theorem 5 asserts that two uses of an additive-noise channel N^{σ²} together with (claimed) Gaussian operations produce a polarized channel with noise σ²e^{-2r} on the clean mode, and the text advocates 'effective quantum communication on the cleaner mode'. Since r is an arbitrary squeezing parameter, this implies that the noise on the useful mode can be made arbitrarily small (→0 as r→∞) from two uses of a fixed noisy channel using only Gaussian resources — an unbounded improvement that contradicts channel-capacity/data-processing limits and the very no-go results cited ([28–31]). The paper provides no analysis bounding this improvement, so the central claim is unsupported.

predicted_errors.error_location: Paragraph after the protocol summary ('our findings do not contravene the main theorem in [31]') vs. title/abstract and the text preceding Corollary 6
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states 'Remarkably, our findings do not contravene the main theorem in [31]', yet the title claims to 'surpass no-go limits', the abstract claims Gaussian QEC 'relies solely on local Gaussian resources', and the text introducing Corollary 6 states 'we can construct a Gaussian entanglement distillation that circumvents the Gaussian QEC no-go result [31]'. These statements are mutually contradictory about whether the no-go theorem is violated or respected.

The protocol is said to apply the polarized channel to σ_AB^{(1)} = (Î_A ⊗ N_B^{σ²})(ρ_ζ) (a pair that already carries noise σ²), yet the stated output is (Î ⊗ N^{e^{-2r}σ²})(ρ_ζ), i.e. the pre-existing σ² noise of pair 1 has been dropped. Composing the two noise processes would give noise σ²(1+e^{-2r}) > σ², which is worse than the input, not 'less noisy'. Either the input must be a locally prepared ideal ρ_ζ (contradicting the notation σ_AB^{(1)} for a shared noisy pair) or the output expression is incorrect.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix F, first line ('We have shown in Eq.(15) that ...')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Appendix F cites Eq. (15) as the derivation of G^{I,N^polar(r)} = G^{σ²Z_2BZ_2S(−r)S^T(−r)Z_2B^TZ_2}, but Eq. (15) in the main text is the GKP logical-noise formula σ_L² = (2σ²/√π)ln(π^{1.5}/(2σ⁴)). The cross-reference points to the wrong equation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Symplectic matrix of the two-mode squeezer S_{j,k}(r) (Gaussian information processing section)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: For Ŝ_{j,k}(r) = e^{r(â_jâ_k − â_j†â_k†)} one obtains Ŝ†â_jŜ = â_j cosh r − â_k† sinh r, giving the symplectic matrix [[cosh(r)I, −sinh(r)Z],[−sinh(r)Z, cosh(r)I]], i.e. the opposite off-diagonal sign to the matrix stated in the text (which corresponds to S_{j,k}(−r)). Consistently, Eq. (4) as written (|ζ_r⟩ with positive tanh^n(r) coefficients) is generated by Ŝ_{1,2}(−r), not Ŝ_{1,2}(r).

predicted_errors.error_location: Definition of the covariance matrix: 'γ(ρ)_{j,k} = tr(ρ x̂_j x̂_k)'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: With [q̂,p̂] = i, tr(ρ x̂_j x̂_k) is neither real nor symmetric (it contains the antisymmetric term (i/2)Ω_{jk}), so it cannot be a covariance matrix of the form used later (real symmetric, transforming as γ → MγM^T + N). The symmetrized definition tr(ρ{x̂_j,x̂_k})/2 is required.
